issue: On plain-error review of a Rehaif claim, may the court of appeals supplement the record under Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 10(e)(2) with evidence the government never introduced in the district court?

sides.position: Yes. Rule 10(e)(2) permits the government to supplement the appellate record with evidence not first introduced in the district court on plain-error Rehaif review, because it is not the government's fault that it did not proffer evidence of the defendant's knowledge of his felon status.
cases: United States v. Lara, 970 F.3d 68 (1st Cir. 2020)
United States v. Miller, 954 F.3d 551 (2d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Brandon, 965 F.3d 427 (5th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Maez, 960 F.3d 949 (7th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Heyward, 42 F.4th 460 (4th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: No. The supplemental evidence was not omitted from the record 'by error or accident' under Rule 10(e)(2), so the court will not consider it on plain-error review.
cases: United States v. Heyward, 42 F.4th 460 (4th Cir. 2022)

quote: Before today, each circuit to have applied this rule to plain-error Rehaif claims permitted the Government to introduce evidence not first introduced in the district court.
cite: United States v. Antwan Heyward, 42 F.4th 460 (4th Cir. 2022)
